market_trends_2025_2026: Platform consolidation: every SAST/SCA incumbent (Checkmarx, Snyk, Veracode, Black Duck, OpenText, HCL, Mend) now sells an ASPM layer, and every pure-play ASPM (Cycode, Apiiro, Legit, OX) has added native scanners. The 'aggregator vs scanner' distinction is collapsing into 'platform with open ingestion'.

Agentic AppSec is the 2026 headline: named agent families are now standard (Checkmarx One Assist, Snyk Evo, ArmorCode Anya with eight roles, Cycode Maestro, Wiz Green/Red/Blue, Phoenix Purple/Green/Blue, Black Duck Signal, GitLab Duo Security Analyst Agent). Forrester's SAST Wave Q3 2025 explicitly called out AI agents and MCP as differentiators.

MCP servers from every vendor: verified MCP servers or MCP-based integrations on Checkmarx, Snyk, GitHub, GitLab, Cycode, Legit, Endor Labs, Semgrep, Phoenix, HCL AppScan, JFrog, Sonatype, Orca, Wiz, DryRun; coding-agent targets are Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Windsurf. Governance of the vendors' own MCP servers is now an evaluation criterion (OWASP MCP guide).

AI-generated code volume drives 'secure at inception' products (Snyk Studio/ADS, Legit VibeGuard, OX VibeSec, Apiiro Guardian Agent, Endor AI Code Governance, Mobb Vibe Shield, Checkmarx Developer Assist) and AI-BOM/AI inventory features (Checkmarx, Apiiro, Black Duck, Mend, JFrog AI Catalog).

Vendor-neutral autofix (Mobb, Pixee, Amplify) is being squeezed as platforms bundle their own autofix and auto-PR agents; the neutral niche survives mainly in heterogeneous scanner estates and backlog burn-down projects.

ASPM absorbed into CNAPP: Wiz (Dazz acquisition Nov 2024, Wiz Code, Google acquisition announced Mar 2025), Palo Alto (Prisma Cloud to Cortex Cloud, 2025), CrowdStrike (Bionic to Falcon ASPM; Gartner Peer Insights Customers' Choice Feb 2026; Pangea acquisition announced Sept 2026), Orca and Sysdig all position code-to-cloud correlation as the ASPM. This creates two ASPM camps: CNAPP-anchored (runtime-first) and SDLC-anchored (code-first).

M&A and private equity: Checkmarx (H&F), Veracode (TA Associates, acquired Longbow 2024 and Phylum 2025), Black Duck (Clearlake/Francisco, carved out Oct 2024), Invicti (Summit; acquired Kondukto 2025), Tromzo now redirecting to Checkmarx (2026, unverified), Jit reportedly acquired by Torq (May 2026, unverified), Cycode acquired Bearer (2024). Expect further pure-play ASPM exits in 2026-2027.

consolidate_vs_best_of_breed.framing: For a consulting delivery team serving multiple clients the question is not one platform for all clients; it is which platform(s) the firm standardises on for its own accelerators, and which neutral layer lets the team operate whatever the client already owns.
arguments_for_consolidation: Single data model, one policy engine and one agent family cut integration and training cost per engagement; Checkmarx One, Snyk and GitLab Ultimate now cover 80-90% of module needs natively.
Autofix and agentic remediation work best when the fixer sees the scanner's own dataflow; cross-vendor autofix is weaker.
Commercial leverage: bundles from Checkmarx, Snyk, Veracode and Black Duck typically discount 25-40% vs buying modules separately (market anecdotes, unverified).
Analyst momentum and client procurement favour vendors present in both the AST and SSCS Magic Quadrants.
arguments_for_best_of_breed_plus_aspm: Client estates are heterogeneous: GitHub/GitLab-native scanning, legacy Fortify, Wiz/Prisma cloud findings, pentest output. A neutral ASPM (ArmorCode, Phoenix, DefectDojo) is the only way to deliver one risk view across clients without forcing scanner replacement.

Module maturity variance inside every platform (DAST and API weak at Checkmarx/Snyk; SAST weak at Wiz/Cortex/Aikido; ASPM ingestion weak at OpenText/HCL) means best-in-class still wins on specific modules.
Lock-in and PE ownership risk: five of the big-six AST vendors are PE-owned; a neutral layer preserves exit options.
Regulated and air-gapped clients need Black Duck, HCL, OpenText, GitLab self-managed or DefectDojo; SaaS-only platforms (Snyk, Cycode, Legit, Wiz) are disqualified for them.
consolidate_vs_best_of_breed.recommendation: Hybrid: standardise the firm's own accelerators on one or two scanner platforms (see contenders) and on a vendor-neutral ASPM/aggregation layer that ingests any client scanner. Keep a benchmarked best-of-breed bench (Semgrep for custom rules, Endor Labs for SCA reachability, Escape for API DAST, Mobb for neutral autofix) for client-specific gaps. Run AI SAST new entrants (ZeroPath, DryRun, Corgea) as second-opinion pilots, not as system of record.

top_3_platform_contenders.tool: ArmorCode (neutral ASPM) paired with GitLab Ultimate or GitHub Advanced Security as the scanner substrate
top_3_platform_contenders.reasoning: For a multi-client consulting team the neutral correlation layer is the strategic asset: ArmorCode's 400+ integrations and Anya agents deliver one risk view over any client's scanners, while GitLab Ultimate (self-managed, air-gap, on-prem AI via self-hosted models) or GHAS ($49/committer/month, high pricing confidence) provide low-friction native scanning. Alternatives with the same shape: Phoenix Security (cheaper, ownership attribution) or Veracode Risk Manager (if the client is already Veracode). Black Duck Polaris + Software Risk Manager is the substitute for air-gapped/SBOM-heavy clients.

best_oss_pick.reasoning: BSD-3 licensed, 200+ parsers, self-hostable and air-gap friendly, the only OSS option that functions as an ASPM/vulnerability-management system of record; paired with Semgrep CE, Trivy, Gitleaks, OWASP ZAP and Syft it yields a zero-licence baseline stack for budget-constrained or sovereignty-constrained clients. Upgrade path to DefectDojo Pro from $100/month. Faraday is the OSS alternative for pentest-centric teams only.
